When Offsite Ads turn a handmade sale into a loss

Sellers search for “are Etsy Offsite Ads worth it” because the fee is easy to miss on a profitable-looking listing. Offsite Ads are charged on the order total (item plus shipping charged), on top of listing, transaction, and payment fees. That is not on-site Etsy Ads. Shops under $10,000 in trailing 12-month sales typically pay 15%; shops over that threshold typically pay 12%. Replace those starting points with the rate on your statement. This page does not opt a shop in or out.

Your numbers stay in this browser. This is arithmetic from your inputs, not Etsy's live Offsite Ads schedule and not a recommendation to opt in or out. Open the order calculator to keep these fees next to Plus, Ads, and free shipping.

Common questions

What is the Etsy Offsite Ads fee?

Etsy Offsite Ads typically charge 15% of the order total for shops under $10,000 in trailing 12-month sales, or 12% for shops over that threshold. The fee applies on top of listing, transaction, and payment-processing fees when Etsy attributes the sale to an offsite ad. Those percentages are starting points you replace with the rate on your statement.

Can Offsite Ads make an Etsy order unprofitable?

Yes. On a $14 handmade print with $3 shipping charged, $5.50 shipping cost, and $7 in materials, the order still clears $2.44 organically and $0.39 at 12%, but loses $0.12 at 15%. Cash invested is $12.50. The order stays at or above $0.00 leftover until Offsite Ads reach about 14.3%.

Are Offsite Ads the same as Etsy Ads?

No. On-site Etsy Ads is a click you buy; ACOS is spend divided by attributed sales. Offsite Ads is a percentage Etsy takes when it sends the buyer from Google or social. They stack. On the calculator's default $30 listing, 15% Offsite Ads still leave $15.98 versus $21.23 organic — the $14 print is the case that flips to a loss.

FOR ETSY SELLERS

Know what each order really leaves.

Enter the fees and costs from your shop to see net profit, margin, return on the cash you put in, and the break-even price before you publish or reprice a listing. Then check whether Etsy Plus credits cover the subscription this month, whether a personalization still pays after extra time and fees, whether on-site Etsy Ads still leave a profit after ACOS, whether Offsite Ads still leave a profit at 12% or 15%, whether a production-partner quote still pays after you run out of handmade hours, whether chasing Star Seller still beats staying unsigned, whether a 20% shop sale still beats staying full price, whether free shipping still leaves a profit, or whether an Etsy shipping label still beats Pirate Ship. Walk the numbers on is Etsy Plus worth it, should I charge for Etsy personalization, is Etsy Ads worth it, are Etsy Offsite Ads worth it, should I use an Etsy production partner, is Etsy Star Seller worth it, should I put my Etsy shop on sale, should I offer free shipping on Etsy, and should I buy Etsy shipping labels. A listing that sells slowly is a different question — does auto-renew still cover the listing fee. The keep-$X price question is what price keeps this leftover after fees. This is not the same job as Etsy's own official fee lookup — this calculator vs. Etsy's own Profit Calculator says which one to open for which question, and this calculator vs. tracking orders in a spreadsheet covers the fee a hand-typed formula usually misses.

Is Etsy Plus worth it this month?

Plus is a monthly subscription. The cash it returns is only the listing credits and Etsy Ads credit you would have paid for anyway — unused credits expire. A custom name, color, or size looks like easy extra cash until Etsy takes a cut of the higher ticket and you spend twenty minutes plus extra supplies. If this buyer would have bought the listing as written, only the extra keep matters. If they would have walked away, the personalized order is extra demand — take it when that path still leaves a profit. This is arithmetic on your inputs, not Etsy's live fee schedule.

Do Offsite Ads still leave a profit?

Offsite Ads are a percentage Etsy takes on the order total when it attributes the sale to Google or social. That is not on-site Etsy Ads — ACOS is a click you buy. Shops under $10,000 in trailing 12-month sales typically pay 15%; shops over that threshold typically pay 12%. The rate in the order form above is your current assumption. This table keeps organic, 12%, and 15% on the same listing. Does this production partner still pay?

A partner quote looks expensive per piece until you run out of hours. Handmade leftover is materials plus your time. The partner path is their all-in unit cost plus handling — they buy the materials. Fees stay the same because the ticket does not change. If you can only make some of the orders you can sell, overflow leftover is $0 unless someone else makes it. Does Star Seller still beat staying unsigned?

The badge is free. The cash it costs is a faster label to stay on-time and the minutes you spend answering messages in 24 hours. The cash it returns is a higher sell-through on the same listings. Message time is paid only on packed sales. Sell-through is what you type from Shop Stats, not a ranking Etsy publishes. Does this shop sale still beat staying full price?

A 20% shop sale looks like a conversion cheat until you keep $5.43 less on every buyer who would have paid full price. The cash it returns is a higher sell-through on the same listings. Percentage fees sit on the lower ticket; postage and materials do not change. This is not free shipping — that zeros shipping charged — and it is not on-site Ads. Does free shipping still leave a profit?

A free-shipping badge looks like a ranking cheat until you keep $2.72 less on every packed order at a $32 item price. Does an Etsy shipping label still beat Pirate Ship?

Buying the label is not the same decision as free shipping or Star Seller. Free shipping is what you charge the buyer. Star Seller is a faster label to stay on-time. Here the shipment is already sold. An Etsy quote auto-uploads tracking and usually keeps a lower item-not-received rate because Purchase Protection rides with the label. A Pirate Ship, Shippo, or carrier-account quote is often cheaper and usually loses that coverage, plus the minutes you spend uploading tracking. A successful claim does not always return every fee Etsy charged on the order — set what share of listing, transaction, payment, and Offsite Ads fees actually comes back below; it defaults to 100% (a full refund) until you change it. Quotes, claim rates, and time are inputs, not a carrier table. Should I buy Etsy shipping labels or use Pirate Ship?

Common questions

What does "Return on cash" measure, and why does it sometimes show "—"?

Return on cash is profit divided by the money you laid out before the sale — shipping cost, materials, and other per-order cost — not divided by revenue or the price you charged. Etsy's fees come out of the proceeds rather than out of your pocket up front, so they stay out of that denominator on purpose. If those three inputs are all zero, there is nothing invested to divide by, so the field reads "—" instead of a divide-by-zero result.

Does the break-even item price include Offsite Ads or on-site Etsy Ads?

It includes whatever offsite ad rate is set on the order form above, spread across the price the same way transaction and payment fees are — raise that rate and the break-even price moves with it. It does not include the separate on-site Etsy Ads section further down the page, because that is a per-click cost you set as an ACOS percentage, not a fee charged on every order.

How does the production partner's reject rate change the comparison?

It reduces how many good units the partner path actually delivers, not the price you pay per unit. At a 5% reject rate, sending 40 orders' worth of demand to the partner yields only 38 sellable units, so the expected cash-out and expected keep per finished sale rise to cover the units that never arrive sellable, on top of the unit cost and handling fee you typed in. Your own handmade capacity and cost are unaffected.

Why is there a separate Offsite Ads table when the order form already has an offsite ad rate field?

The order form's rate is your current best guess and feeds every other number on the page — the hero result, break-even price, and every comparison table. The Offsite Ads section further down re-runs that same order at organic (0%), 12%, and 15% side by side, because Etsy sets the rate by a shop's trailing 12-month sales rather than letting a seller choose it, so seeing all three shows what changes if a shop crosses that threshold.

Does anything typed into this calculator leave the browser?

No. Every figure is computed locally; nothing is sent to a server. Inputs are saved to this browser's local storage so the form survives a reload, and "Copy shareable link" puts them in the URL instead so a specific scenario can be sent to someone else. Anonymous local feature-usage counts are recorded unless "Do not keep anonymous local usage counts" below is checked.

← Etsy profit calculator

Is Etsy Ads worth it?

Sellers search for “is Etsy Ads worth it” because a 12% ACOS looks cheap next to a $30 sale. ACOS is spend divided by attributed sales — $4.20 on a $35 order. That cash leaves whether or not the buyer would have found you anyway. Offsite Ads is a different fee: a percentage Etsy takes when it sends the buyer.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and type the ACOS from Ads Manager. Monthly spend is the same figure as the Plus table. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 postage, $4.00 materials, 12% ACOS, $5.00 monthly Ads spend.

A 12% ACOS still leaves $17.03 on an extra order

The organic sale keeps $21.23. The advertised sale keeps $17.03 after a $4.20 Ads cost — $4.20 less (−$4.20). An extra advertised order still pays until ACOS reaches about 60.64%. A $5.00 monthly budget at this ACOS buys about 1.19 advertised orders and keeps $20.27 if they are incremental.

PathAds on this orderFeesKept
Organic sale$0.00$3.78$21.23
Advertised sale$4.20$3.78$17.03

A 70% ACOS loses money even as extra demand

Raise ACOS to 70% on the same order and Ads cost $24.50. The advertised sale keeps $-3.27 (−$3.27) even if the click is extra demand you would not have sold otherwise. The ceiling stays 60.64% — that is leftover profit divided by order revenue, not a fee Etsy publishes.

Offsite Ads lower the ACOS you can still carry

Turn on 15% Offsite Ads and keep the 12% ACOS. Organic keep falls to $15.98. Advertised keep falls to $11.78 after the same $4.20 click. The ACOS ceiling drops to about 45.64%. Offsite Ads and Etsy Ads stack; they are not substitutes.

If they would have bought anyway

That is a cannibalized sale. On the 12% example Ads cost you $4.20 versus the organic $21.23. Take the click when it is extra demand and the advertised path still leaves a profit.

Rates change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live Ads CPC or Offsite Ads schedule. Enter the ACOS and fees from your last statement and Ads Manager.

Common questions

Is Etsy Ads worth it?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, and a 12% ACOS — the organic sale keeps $21.23. The advertised sale keeps $17.03 after a $4.20 Ads cost. An extra advertised order still pays until ACOS reaches about 60.64%. A $5.00 monthly budget at 12% ACOS buys about 1.19 advertised orders and keeps $20.27 if they are incremental.

Are Etsy Ads the same as Offsite Ads?

No. On-site Etsy Ads is a click you buy; ACOS is spend divided by attributed sales. Offsite Ads is a percentage Etsy takes when it sends the buyer from Google or social. Enter both. Raising Offsite Ads to 15% on the same 12% ACOS drops organic keep to $15.98, advertised keep to $11.78, and the ACOS ceiling to about 45.64%.

What if the Ads click would have bought anyway?

That is a cannibalized sale. On the 12% example Ads cost you $4.20 versus the organic $21.23. Take the click when it is extra demand and the advertised path still leaves a profit. A 70% ACOS on the same order costs $24.50 and loses $3.27 even if the click is extra demand.

is-etsy-plus-worth-it.html.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Is Etsy Plus worth it this month?

Sellers search for “is Etsy Plus worth it” because the $10.00 subscription looks cheap next to a pile of $0.20 listing fees. The cash Plus returns is only the credits you would have paid for anyway. Unused credits expire. Shop banners and restock requests are not a fee discount unless you assign them a dollar value.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your listing fee, and enter how many listings you will create or renew and how much Etsy Ads you would buy without Plus. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $0.20 listing fee, 15 listing credits, $5.00 Ads credit, $10.00 Plus fee.

Use every credit, spend the Ads credit anyway

Fifteen listings and $5.00 of Ads you would have bought: stay off Plus and you pay $8.00. Subscribe and you pay $10.00. Plus costs $2.00 more (−$2.00). The included credits are worth at most $8.00 against a $10.00 fee, so volume past 15 listings cannot close the gap — those extra listings cost $0.20 on both paths.

PathListing feesAds you payPlus feeCash out
Stay off Plus$3.00$5.00$0.00$8.00
Etsy Plus$0.00$0.00$10.00$10.00

Five renewals and no Ads

Five listings and $0.00 Ads: stay off Plus and you pay $1.00. Subscribe and you pay $10.00. Plus costs $9.00 more (−$9.00). Ten listing credits ($2.00) and $5.00 of Ads credit expire unused.

When Plus can keep more cash

If you assign $3.00 to Plus shop features on top of the same 15 listings and $5.00 Ads spend, Plus keeps $1.00 more (+$1.00). If your listing fee is $1.00 and you use all 15 credits with no Ads, stay off Plus costs $15.00 and Plus costs $10.00, so Plus keeps $5.00 more (+$5.00).

Rates and credits change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live Plus schedule. Enter the numbers from your own Plus invoice and Ads dashboard. The calculator is arithmetic, not advice, and it does not claim Plus will raise your search rank or sales.

Common questions

Is Etsy Plus worth it if I use every credit?

At a $0.20 listing fee, 15 listing credits and a $5 Ads credit are worth $8 against a $10 Plus fee. If you would have paid for those listings and that Ads spend anyway, Plus still costs $2.00 more this month. Extra listings past the 15-credit cap cost the same on both paths.

Do unused Etsy Plus credits roll over?

No. Unused listing credits and unused Ads credit expire at the end of the billing cycle. A shop that renews five listings and runs no Ads keeps only $1.00 of credit value and pays $10.00, so Plus costs $9.00 more that month.

Does Etsy Plus lower transaction fees?

No. Plus does not change Etsy's transaction or payment-processing rates. It is a subscription with listing credits, an Ads credit, and shop-customization features. Offsite Ads are a separate sale fee and are not the Plus Ads credit.

is-etsy-star-seller-worth-it.html.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Is Etsy Star Seller worth it?

Sellers search for “is Etsy Star Seller worth it” because the badge looks free. It is free. The cash it costs is a faster label to stay on-time and the minutes you spend answering messages in 24 hours. The cash it returns is a higher sell-through on the same listings.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and type the postage you would buy to stay on-time plus the sell-through from Shop Stats. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 unsigned postage, $9.00 Star Seller postage, $4.00 materials, 8 minutes at $18/hour, 40% vs 50% sell-through, 40 listings.

A 10-point lift still loses $0.58 after the faster label

A packed unsigned sale keeps $21.23. A packed Star Seller sale, after $3.00 extra postage and $2.40 answering messages, keeps $15.83. At 40.0% vs 50.0% sell-through the unsigned path expects $8.49 per listing and Star Seller expects $7.91 — $0.58 less (−$0.58, −$23.20 across 40 listings). The badge has to convert about 53.6% of listings before it matches staying unsigned. Star Seller postage has to stay at or below about $7.85 at this conversion lift.

PathPacked leftoverSell-throughExpected / listingAcross 40 listings
Stay unsigned$21.2340.0%$8.49$339.60
Chase Star Seller$15.8350.0%$7.91$316.40

A 20-point lift flips the badge ahead

Raise Star Seller sell-through to 60% on the same fees. Expected keep becomes $9.50 — +$1.01 per listing, +$40.40 across 40 listings. The break-even conversion stays 53.6%; a bigger lift just clears it. A shop converting only 20% that lifts to 35% expects $4.25 unsigned vs $5.54 with the badge (+$1.29).

A $7.00 Star Seller label covers a 10-point lift

Keep 40% vs 50% and drop Star Seller postage to $7.00. The packed Star Seller sale keeps $17.83 after $3.40 extra cash. Expected keep is +$0.42 versus staying unsigned. The postage ceiling on the default lift stays about $7.85 — above that, the faster label plus message time costs more than a 10-point lift returns.

A shop that already converts does not need the badge

A shop already converting 70% that only lifts to 75% expects $14.86 unsigned vs $11.87 with Star Seller (−$2.99). Extra postage and message time wipe a small lift. Type the sell-through you actually see, not the badge’s best week.

Rules change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live Star Seller criteria, search ranking, or label prices. Enter the postage you would buy and the conversion from Shop Stats.

Common questions

Is Etsy Star Seller worth it?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 unsigned postage vs a $9 Star Seller label, $4 materials, 8 minutes at $18/hour, and 40% vs 50% sell-through — a packed unsigned sale keeps $21.23 and a packed Star Seller sale keeps $15.83. Expected keep is $8.49 vs $7.91, which is $0.58 less per listing and $23.20 less across 40 listings. The badge has to convert about 53.6% before it matches staying unsigned. Star Seller postage has to stay at or below about $7.85 at this lift.

When does a bigger conversion lift make Star Seller pay?

A 20-point lift from 40% to 60% on the same fees flips Star Seller ahead by $1.01 per listing ($40.40 across 40 listings). A shop converting only 20% that lifts to 35% keeps $1.29 more with the badge. A shop already converting 70% that only lifts to 75% still loses $2.99 per listing — the extra postage and message time wipe a small lift.

Does a cheaper Star Seller label change the answer?

Yes. Keep the 40% vs 50% lift and drop Star Seller postage to $7.00. The packed Star Seller sale keeps $17.83 and expected keep is $0.42 more than staying unsigned. The postage ceiling on the default lift stays about $7.85 — above that, the 10-point lift does not cover the faster label plus message time.

Does auto-renew still pay if this listing is slow?

Etsy charges the listing fee when a listing publishes or auto-renews — not once per sale. The order calculator subtracts that fee from every order. This page allocates it across the sales you actually expect in one renewal window, including zero. It does not turn auto-renew on or off.

Common questions

Does Etsy auto-renew still pay if a listing is slow?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, $1 other cost, a $0.20 listing fee, and a 4-month renewal window — contribution before the listing fee is $20.43. Two sales leave $40.65 after the listing fee ($0.10 per sale). One sale recovers the fee. Charging $0.20 on every order overstates listing cost by $0.20 across those two sales.

What does auto-renew cost if nothing sells?

Zero sales still leave −$0.20 after the listing fee. Treating the listing fee as a per-order cost hides that $0.20 until an order is calculated. At a 4-month window the listing still costs $0.60 a year.

Does the order calculator already include the listing fee?

Yes, once per order. That is right for a listing that sells once and wrong for one that sells five times ($0.04 listing cost per sale) or zero times. This page keeps the same fee stack, then allocates the listing fee across the sales you type in. It does not turn auto-renew on or off.

Should I buy Etsy shipping labels or use Pirate Ship?

Sellers search for “Etsy shipping labels vs Pirate Ship” because the cheaper quote looks like free leftover. It is not. Four minutes to buy and upload a label plus a higher item-not-received rate usually eat a $0.90 postage save.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and type the Etsy quote and the Pirate Ship, Shippo, or carrier-account quote you would actually buy. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 Etsy label, $5.10 third-party label, 0.8% vs 2.5% claims, 4 minutes at $18/hour, 40 shipments/month.

This is not free shipping — that is what you charge the buyer — and it is not Star Seller. Purchase Protection, label quotes, and claim rates are inputs, not Etsy’s live policy.

Four minutes wipe a $0.90 postage save

The $6.00 Etsy label at a 0.8% claim rate expects $20.98 after the typed claim mix — a claim on that path leaves −$10.00. A $5.10 third-party label at a 2.5% claim rate after $1.20 of upload time expects $20.14 (−$0.84 per shipment, −$33.60 across 40). The same third-party postage with no extra time expects $21.34 (+$0.36). No third-party claim rate on the timed path can match the Etsy label. The quote has to stay at about $4.27 before it matches.

PathLabelExtra timePacked leftoverExpected keep
Etsy label$6.00—$21.23$20.98
Third-party label$5.10$1.20$20.93$20.14
Third-party, no extra time$5.10—$22.13$21.34

Zero upload minutes flip Pirate Ship ahead by $0.36

Keep the default fees and drop upload time to zero. The $5.10 quote expects $21.34 — $0.36 more than Etsy’s $20.98. Third-party claims then have to stay at about 3.7% before that path matches. Matching the 0.8% Etsy claim rate and keeping the four minutes still loses −$0.30 ($20.68 vs $20.98). A $4.00 quote and one upload minute expects $22.14 (+$1.16).

15% Offsite Ads still leave the Etsy label ahead

Turn on 15% Offsite Ads and keep the default labels. The Etsy label expects $15.77. The timed third-party path expects $15.03 (−$0.74). Postage-only expects $16.23. The cheaper quote still loses after four minutes.

Rules change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live Shipping rates, Purchase Protection rules, or carrier tables. Enter the quotes from the labels you would actually buy.

Common questions

Should I buy Etsy shipping labels or use Pirate Ship?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6.00 Etsy label, $5.10 third-party label, 0.8% vs 2.5% item-not-received claims, and 4 minutes at $18/hour — the Etsy label expects $20.98. The timed third-party path expects $20.14 (−$0.84, −$33.60 across 40 shipments). The same third-party postage with no extra time expects $21.34 (+$0.36). Four minutes wipe a $0.90 postage save. The third-party quote has to stay at about $4.27 before the timed path matches Etsy.

When does Pirate Ship beat an Etsy shipping label?

When upload time is already sunk and the claim-rate gap stays small. Drop the four minutes to zero on the same $30 listing and the $5.10 quote expects $21.34 — $0.36 more than Etsy’s $20.98. Third-party claims then have to stay at about 3.7% before that path matches. A $4.00 quote and one upload minute expects $22.14 (+$1.16). Matching the 0.8% Etsy claim rate and keeping the four minutes still loses $0.30.

Is this the same as free shipping or Star Seller?

No. Free shipping is what you charge the buyer. Star Seller is a faster label to stay on-time plus message time. This page is where you buy the already-sold tracked label: Etsy Shipping versus Pirate Ship, Shippo, or a carrier account, after the claim rate that usually moves with Purchase Protection and the minutes you spend uploading tracking.

should-i-charge-for-etsy-personalization.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Should I charge for Etsy personalization?

Sellers search for “should I charge for Etsy personalization” because an $8.00 name, color, or size add-on looks like free margin. Transaction and payment fees sit on the higher ticket. Extra thread, ink, or a gift box is cash out. Twenty minutes at $18/hour is $6.00 you will not get back.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and enter the upcharge and extras for the request in front of you. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 postage, $4.00 materials, $8.00 personalization, $1.50 extra materials, $6.00 extra time.

The $8 add-on loses against the standard sale

Selling as listed keeps $21.23. Taking the custom request keeps $20.97. Personalization keeps $0.26 less (−$0.26). Extra fees on the higher ticket are $0.76. Extra cash out is $7.50. Across 12 custom orders that is −$3.12. The upcharge has to reach about $8.29 before the upgrade beats the standard sale.

PathItem priceFeesExtra cash outKept
Sell as listed$30.00$3.78$0.00$21.23
Take the personalization$38.00$4.54$7.50$20.97

Ignore time and the same $8 keeps more

If you treat extra time as $0.00 and still spend $1.50 on materials, the same $8.00 personalization keeps $26.97 — $5.74 more than the $21.23 standard sale (+$5.74). The break-even upcharge falls to about $1.66. That is why a shop that “doesn’t count time” thinks every custom request is free money.

Charge $12 and the upgrade wins

A $12.00 upcharge on the same extras keeps $24.59 — $3.36 more than selling as listed (+$3.36), or $40.32 across 12 custom orders. Raise Offsite Ads to 15% on the original $8.00 add-on and extra fees become $1.96, the upgrade loses $1.46 (−$1.46), and the break-even upcharge rises to about $9.93.

If they would not have bought the standard listing

That is extra demand. On the default $8.00 request the personalized order still leaves $20.97 versus $0.00. Take it when that path is still a profit, even if the upgrade loses against a standard sale you would have made anyway.

Rates change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live fee schedule. Enter the numbers from your last payout and the request in front of you. The calculator is arithmetic, not advice, and it does not claim a personalization will raise your conversion or search rank.

Common questions

Should I charge for Etsy personalization?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, an $8.00 personalization, $1.50 extra materials, and $6.00 extra time — selling as listed keeps $21.23. Taking the custom request keeps $20.97, which is $0.26 less. Extra fees on the higher ticket are $0.76. The upcharge has to reach about $8.29 before the upgrade beats the standard sale.

Does Etsy take fees on a personalization add-on?

Transaction, payment-processing, and Offsite Ads percentages sit on item plus shipping, so they rise with the upcharge. The listing fee and the payment fixed fee do not change. Enter the rates from your last payout; this page does not claim Etsy's live schedule.

What if the buyer would not have bought the standard listing?

That is extra demand. On the same defaults the personalized order still leaves $20.97 versus $0.00 if you decline. Take the request when that path is still a profit, even if the upgrade loses against a standard sale you would have made anyway.

should-i-offer-free-shipping-on-etsy.htm.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Should I offer free shipping on Etsy?

Sellers search for “should I offer free shipping on Etsy” because the badge looks like a ranking cheat. It is not free. Every packed order at a $32 item price leaves $2.72 less than charging $5.00 shipping on a $30 listing. The cash free shipping returns is extra orders, not a cheaper fee stack.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and type the free-shipping item price you would actually list. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 postage, $4.00 materials, $32.00 free-shipping price, 40 orders/month.

This is not a shop sale — that discounts the ticket while still charging shipping — and it is not on-site Etsy Ads. Percentage fees sit on the customer total. Postage and materials do not change.

A $32 free-shipping price needs about 5.9 extra orders

Charging $5.00 shipping on a $30.00 item leaves $21.23 per order. Free shipping at the same item price leaves $16.70 (−$4.53). Moving the label into the item price ($35.00 + $0.00) leaves $21.23 — the same customer total is a tie. Free shipping at $32.00 leaves $18.51 (−$2.72 per order). At 40 orders/month, free shipping needs about 5.9 extra orders (14.7%) to match $849.00.

PathItem + shipping chargedKept / orderThis month
Charge shipping$30.00 + $5.00$21.23$849.00
Free shipping, same item price$30.00 + $0.00$16.70$668.00
Free shipping, same customer total$35.00 + $0.00$21.23$849.00
Free shipping at $32.00$32.00 + $0.00$18.51$740.40

Eating the label needs 10.8 extra orders; $40 already wins

Keep the default fees and drop the free-shipping price to $30.00. Leftover becomes $16.70 (−$4.53). That path needs about 10.8 extra orders (27.1%) to match charging shipping. Raise the free-shipping price to $40.00 and leftover becomes $25.75 (+$4.52). Free shipping already keeps more per order, so it does not need extra volume.

Offsite Ads raise the lift to 6.6 extra orders

Turn on 15% Offsite Ads and keep the $32.00 path. Charging shipping keeps $15.98. Free shipping keeps $13.71 (−$2.27). The lift rises to about 6.6 extra orders (16.5%) to match $639.00.

Rules change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live shipping schedule, search ranking, or free-shipping badge rules. Enter the item price you would actually list and the order count from Shop Stats.

Common questions

Should I offer free shipping on Etsy?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, and a $32 free-shipping item price at 40 orders/month — charging shipping keeps $21.23. Free shipping at the same $30 item price keeps $16.70 (−$4.53). Moving the label into the item price ($35.00 + $0.00) keeps $21.23 — a tie. Free shipping at $32.00 keeps $18.51 (−$2.72 per order). It needs about 5.9 extra orders (14.7%) to match $849.00.

Is absorbing the shipping charge into the item price free?

Yes on the fee stack. Percentage fees sit on item price plus shipping charged, so $30 + $5.00 and $35.00 + $0.00 leave the same $21.23. Extra leftover only appears when the customer total changes, or when free shipping brings more orders.

Does Offsite Ads change how many extra orders free shipping needs?

Yes. Turn on 15% Offsite Ads on the same $32 path. Charging shipping keeps $15.98; free shipping keeps $13.71 (−$2.27). The lift rises to about 6.6 extra orders (16.5%). A $40 free-shipping price already keeps $25.75 (+$4.52) and does not need extra volume. Eating the label at $30 needs about 10.8 extra orders (27.1%).

should-i-put-my-etsy-shop-on-sale.html.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Should I put my Etsy shop on sale?

Sellers search for “should I put my Etsy shop on sale” because a 20% coupon looks like a conversion cheat. It is not free. Every buyer who would have paid full price leaves $5.43 less on the default $30 listing. The cash a sale returns is a higher sell-through on the same listings.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and type the percent or dollar coupon you would run plus the sell-through from Shop Stats. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 postage, $4.00 materials, 20% off vs $5.00 off, 40% vs 55% sell-through, 40 listings.

This is not free shipping — that zeros shipping charged — and it is not on-site Etsy Ads. Percentage fees sit on the lower ticket; postage and materials do not change.

A 15-point lift makes $5 off beat 20% and full price

A packed full-price sale keeps $21.23. 20% off drops the ticket to $24.00 and leaves $15.80 if this buyer would have paid full price (−$5.43). A $5.00 coupon leaves $16.70 (−$4.53 vs full price). At 40.0% vs 55.0% sell-through the full-price path expects $8.49 per listing, 20% off expects $8.69 (+$0.20, +$8.00 across 40 listings), and $5.00 off expects $9.19 (+$0.70, +$28.00 across 40 listings). 20% off has to convert about 53.8% of listings before it matches staying full price. The dollar coupon has to convert about 50.8%. At this lift the sale has to stay at or below about 21.3% or $6.40 off.

PathPacked leftoverSell-throughExpected / listingAcross 40 listings
Stay full price$21.2340.0%$8.49$339.60
20% off$15.8055.0%$8.69$347.60
$5.00 off$16.7055.0%$9.19$367.60

A 10-point lift is not enough — stay full price

Keep 20% and $5.00 off and drop sale sell-through to 50%. Expected keep becomes $7.90 on 20% off (−$0.59, −$23.60 across 40 listings) and $8.35 on $5.00 off (−$0.14, −$5.60). Stay full price. The break-even conversion stays 53.8% for 20% off and 50.8% for $5.00 off — a 10-point lift does not clear either. Raise sale sell-through to 70% and $5.00 off expects $11.69 (+$3.20) while 20% off expects $11.06 (+$2.57).

Offsite Ads make 20% lose; a 10% sale keeps more than $5 off

Turn on 15% Offsite Ads and keep the 40% vs 55% lift. Full price expects $6.39, 20% off expects $6.29 (−$0.10), and $5.00 off expects $6.71 (+$0.32). 20% off now has to convert about 55.8%; the discount ceiling falls to about 19.2% or $5.77 off. Drop the percent sale to 10% on the default fees (no Offsite Ads) and the packed sale keeps $18.51. Expected keep is $10.18 — +$1.69 versus full price — and 10% off beats the $5.00 coupon too.

Rules change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live coupon schedule, search ranking, or sale calendar. Enter the discount you would actually run and the conversion from Shop Stats.

Common questions

Should I put my Etsy shop on sale?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, 20% off vs $5.00 off, and 40% vs 55% sell-through — a packed full-price sale keeps $21.23, 20% off keeps $15.80 (−$5.43 if this buyer would have paid full price), and $5.00 off keeps $16.70 (−$4.53). Expected keep is $8.49 vs $8.69 vs $9.19. The $5 coupon expects $0.70 more per listing and $28.00 more across 40 listings. 20% off has to convert about 53.8% before it matches staying full price; $5 off has to convert about 50.8%. At this lift the sale has to stay at or below about 21.3% or $6.40 off.

Is a 10-point conversion lift enough to run a sale?

No. Keep 20% and $5.00 off and drop sale sell-through to 50%. Expected keep becomes $7.90 on 20% off (−$0.59) and $8.35 on $5.00 off (−$0.14). Stay full price. The break-even conversion stays 53.8% for 20% off and 50.8% for $5.00 off — a 10-point lift does not clear either.

Does Offsite Ads change which sale still pays?

Yes. Turn on 15% Offsite Ads on the same 40% vs 55% lift. Full price expects $6.39, 20% off expects $6.29 (−$0.10), and $5.00 off expects $6.71 (+$0.32). 20% off now has to convert about 55.8%; the discount ceiling falls to about 19.2% or $5.77 off. A shallower 10% sale on the default fees, with no Offsite Ads, keeps $18.51 packed and expects $10.18 — $1.69 more than full price, beating the $5 coupon too.

should-i-use-an-etsy-production-partner..text:
← Etsy profit calculator

Should I use an Etsy production partner?

Sellers search for “should I use an Etsy production partner” because a $14.00 all-in quote looks like it kills margin. Handmade leftover is materials plus the time it actually takes you. The partner path is their unit cost plus handling — they buy the materials. Fees stay the same because the ticket does not change. The part most shops miss is capacity: leftover on the orders you cannot make is $0.00.

Open the Etsy profit calculator, keep your shop fees, and enter the quote and the hours you actually have. The table below uses the calculator defaults: $30 item, $5.00 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction, 3% + $0.25 payment, $6.00 postage, $4.00 materials, $8.00 of your time, a $14.00 partner quote, $1.00 handling, 20 units you can make, and 40 you can sell.

The $14 quote loses per piece and still wins the month

Making it yourself keeps $13.23 per order. The $14.00 partner quote, after $1.00 handling, keeps $10.23 — $3.00 less per sale (−$3.00). You can only make 20 of the 40 you can sell, so staying handmade leaves $264.60 this month. Sending every order to the partner leaves $409.20. Making what you can and sending the overflow keeps $469.20 — $204.60 more than staying handmade (+$204.60). The partner quote has to fall to about $11.00 before it matches your handmade leftover. Raising the listing to about $33.32 keeps the handmade leftover on the partner path.

PathUnitsCash out / saleKept / saleThis month
You make them20$12.00$13.23$264.60
Partner makes them40$15.00$10.23$409.20
You make what you can, partner the rest40$13.50$11.73$469.20

A $10 quote beats handmade on the unit and the month

Drop the partner quote to $10.00 and keep the $1.00 handling. That path keeps $14.23 — $1.00 more than handmade (+$1.00). Sending every order leaves $569.20 this month. Hybrid leftover is $549.20 because you would still be making the expensive units yourself. If the quote is cheaper than your materials plus time, send the whole book.

Rejected units still cost you

A 10% reject rate on the original $14.00 quote raises the effective cost per sale to $16.67 and drops leftover to $8.56. The break-even quote falls to about $9.80. Enter the reject rate from the last batch, not a hope. This page does not claim a partner will match your finish or that Etsy will keep the listing in Handmade.

When you can already fill the book

If you can sell only 15 and you can make 20, overflow is not a path. Handmade leftover this month is $198.45. The partner path is $153.45. Stay handmade until demand outruns your hours.

Rates change. This page does not publish Etsy’s live fee schedule. Enter the numbers from your last payout and the quote in front of you. The calculator is arithmetic, not advice, and it does not claim a production partner will raise your conversion or search rank.

Common questions

Should I use an Etsy production partner?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, $8.00 of your time, a $14.00 all-in partner quote, and $1.00 handling — handmade keeps $13.23 per order. The partner path keeps $10.23, which is $3.00 less per sale. You can only make 20 of the 40 you can sell, so staying handmade leaves $264.60 this month. Sending every order to the partner leaves $409.20. Making what you can and sending the overflow keeps $469.20.

Does a cheaper partner quote beat handmade per unit?

Yes, when the all-in quote plus handling falls below your materials plus time. On the same fees a $10.00 partner quote keeps $14.23 — $1.00 more than handmade — and $569.20 this month if you send every order. The default $14.00 quote has to fall to about $11.00 before it matches your handmade leftover.

What if some partner units are unsellable?

You still paid for them. A 10% reject rate on the $14.00 quote raises the effective cost per sale to $16.67 and drops leftover to $8.56. The break-even quote falls to about $9.80. Enter the reject rate from the last batch, not a hope.

vs-a-spreadsheet.html.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

This calculator vs. tracking Etsy orders in a spreadsheet

A spreadsheet is where most sellers already track price, materials, and quantity, and it stays the record you own -- this page is not an argument against keeping one. What a spreadsheet usually does not have is a column for Offsite Ads: a fee that applies per order, not per listing, and that Etsy does not flag on the order itself. A seller typing a single blended "Etsy fee %" into a spreadsheet column -- set once from a past statement, covering the listing, transaction, and payment-processing fees that are the same on every order -- has no row for the order Etsy attributes to an Offsite Ads click, because that attribution is not visible until the statement totals it up weeks later.

A worked example, computed from this calculator's own arithmetic: a $45 item with $6.50 shipping charged, $5.00 shipping cost, and $12.00 in materials. A spreadsheet using the blended 9.5% rate (6.5% transaction + 3% payment) plus the $0.20 listing fee and $0.25 payment fixed fee computes a profit of $29.16. If Etsy attributes this particular sale to an Offsite Ads click at the published 15% rate, the order actually keeps $21.43 -- the spreadsheet's number was $7.73 higher than what actually landed, a 36% overstatement on this one order, and the spreadsheet has no column that would have caught it.

What a spreadsheet usually doesWhat this calculator does
One hand-typed "Etsy fee %" column, covering the fees that are the same on every order. Every fee an order can carry computed from the current rates you enter -- listing, transaction, payment processing, and Offsite Ads.
No field for Offsite Ads, because the order itself does not say whether Etsy attributed the sale to that channel. Offsite Ads priced at organic, 12%, and 15% side by side, so the gap between "if this order is organic" and "if it isn't" is visible before the statement lands.
A new formula to write, copy down, and re-check for each follow-on question -- Etsy Plus, Star Seller, a shop sale, a production partner. Nine follow-on decisions already built in, each on the same shop numbers -- see the FAQ on the main page.
Stays private if you keep it that way, but has to be rebuilt or copied to share a scenario with anyone else. A shareable link that carries your inputs after the # in the URL -- never uploaded anywhere, reproduced only in whoever's browser opens that link.

This tool needs no Etsy account, no shop sign-in, and no spreadsheet software: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off. Nothing you type is uploaded anywhere.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or keep tracking orders in my own spreadsheet?

Most sellers get more use out of both. A spreadsheet is where you already track price, cost, and quantity, and it stays the record you own. What it usually does not have is a column for Offsite Ads, because that fee applies per order rather than per listing and Etsy does not flag which sale it hit until the monthly statement arrives -- so most spreadsheets either ignore it or use last month's blended rate, and both read as profit that was never actually kept. This calculator prices every fee an order can carry, including Offsite Ads at organic, 12%, and 15% side by side, so the gap is visible before the statement lands, not after.

Why does a spreadsheet usually miss the Offsite Ads fee specifically?

Because nothing on the order itself says it was an Offsite Ads sale. A seller typing a blended fee percentage into a spreadsheet column has one number for every row, set from a past statement or a remembered rate -- typically the listing, transaction, and payment-processing fees a seller checks often. Offsite Ads is a separate, per-order fee (12% or 15% of the order, depending on trailing shop sales) that Etsy applies only when it attributes a sale to that channel, and the attribution is not visible on the order until the statement totals it up weeks later.

Is this page affiliated with Etsy?

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Etsy, Inc. Etsy and Offsite Ads are trademarks of Etsy, Inc. or its affiliates, named here only to describe what this calculator is for.

Open the Etsy profit calculator to run the comparison on your own numbers.

vs-etsys-listing-form-calculator.html.text:
← Etsy profit calculator

This calculator vs. Etsy's own Profit Calculator

Etsy publishes its own free estimator for sellers, built directly into the listing form. Etsy's Seller Handbook describes it in "Easily Estimate Your Profits With Our New Profit Calculator": open the Price & inventory section while creating or editing a listing on desktop or mobile web, enter the price and the costs that go into the item — materials, labor, packaging, marketing, and any shipping not covered by the buyer — and it estimates the listing, payment-processing, and transaction fees that listing will owe when it sells.

That makes it the right tool for one job: a quick check on the one listing you are pricing, without leaving the listing form. Etsy's own handbook article notes a real limit on it, too — it does not include fees that vary per order, so an Offsite Ads sale (which adds a fee) or a Share & Save sale (which discounts one) will not match the estimate. It also is not yet available inside the Etsy Seller app, only the desktop and mobile web listing form.

QuestionWhere to answer it
What will this one listing roughly net, right while I'm pricing it? Etsy's own Profit Calculator — built into the listing form.
What does an order actually leave after my shop's whole fee stack, including an Offsite Ads order? This calculator — Offsite Ads at organic, 12%, and 15% side by side, and every fee visible at once. It has no Share & Save field; a Share & Save order prices the same here as an ordinary one.
What price hits a target margin or a target dollar profit? This calculator's repricer, next to the order result.
Does Etsy Plus, Star Seller, a shop sale, free shipping, a production partner, a personalization, or an Etsy shipping label still pay on this same shop? This calculator's linked sections — see the FAQ on the main page.

Beyond the fee comparison, this tool also keeps your shop's numbers saved in your own browser between visits, and a shareable link that carries your inputs after the # in the URL — never uploaded anywhere, and reproduced only in whoever's browser opens that link.

This tool needs no Etsy account, no shop sign-in, and no listing to exist yet: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off. Nothing you type is uploaded anywhere.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or Etsy's own Profit Calculator?

Most sellers get more use out of both. Etsy's own Profit Calculator, built into the Price & Inventory section of the listing form, is the fastest place to sanity-check one listing while you are pricing it, right where you already are. This page does not try to replace that. What it adds is everything that tool is not built around: the whole shop's fee stack on one screen, a break-even price and target-margin repricer, saved and shareable scenarios, and nine follow-on decisions on the same listing, from whether Etsy Plus pays for itself to whether Star Seller beats staying unsigned, none of which are a single-listing fee estimate.

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Etsy, Inc. Etsy, Etsy Plus, Star Seller, and Offsite Ads are trademarks of Etsy, Inc. or its affiliates, named here only to describe what this calculator is for.

Common questions

What Etsy price keeps $20 after fees?

On the worked example — a $30 listing, $5 shipping charged, 6.5% transaction plus 3%+$0.25 payment, $6 postage, $4 materials, and a $0.20 listing fee — leftover at $30 is $21.23. The item price that keeps $20 after those same fees is $28.65. $10 leftover is $17.60. $30 leftover is $39.70.

Does this recommend a price?

No. It is the inverse of the order calculator: same fee stack, solved for item price instead of leftover. It does not publish Etsy's live schedule and does not say you should raise or lower a listing.

Where is target profit on the main calculator?

The order calculator already has a Target profit per order field under Reprice for a goal. This page is the same arithmetic on its own landing so the keep-$X question is searchable and shareable without the rest of the fee stack.
